episode: Building the Automated AGI Lab: Core Automation's Jerry Tworek and Rohan Anil
what: They argue that the transformer architecture has reached its limits and that future AGI progress hinges on new architectures enabling continual learning. They critique in-context learning and fine-tuning as insufficient, and propose end-to-end optimization of pre-training and reinforcement learning.
why: This is a foundational critique of current AI scaling strategies and a rare technical roadmap for post-transformer systems. Core Automation’s approach could shape the next wave of AI infrastructure.

what: Ben Horowitz discusses the critical importance of open-source AI for innovation, security, and competition. He warns against the monopolization of AI by a few frontier labs, explores the economics of frontier models, and touches on distillation, robotics, and the cultural implications of AI-generated art.
why: This is a high-level strategic conversation on the future of AI ecosystems, platform economics, and long-term capital allocation in the AI stack.

episode: Dianne Penn on Anthropic's technical PM role
what: Dianne, Anthropic’s first technical PM, shares insights into the company’s early days, the development of Claude models, eval-driven development loops, and how the team built superior coding capabilities. She also discusses the challenges of building AI systems that can push back and maintain alignment.
why: Offers a rare operational view into how top-tier AI labs ship and iterate models — valuable for understanding product-market fit in AI infrastructure and platform development.

She joined in 2023 as Anthropic’s first technical product manager, when the entire product team was five engineers, and has since helped ship every model from Claude 2 through Fable, and helped incubate Claude Code, MCP, Skills, computer use, tool use, and reasoning. Before Anthropic, she helped build Alexa’s AI at Amazon and, before that, traded high-yield bonds at JP Morgan Chase.
